mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes CLK 270/320 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mercedes CLK 270 CDI or CLK 320 CDI replacement engine typically costs between £1,000 for a used unit and £3,200 for a fully rebuilt engine. Specialist fitting adds £400-£800. Used OM612/OM642 engines: £1,000-£2,200 depending on mileage and condition. Reconditioned units: £1,300-£2,800 supply only. Rebuilt units: £1,600-£3,200 with 12-month warranty. Specialist fitting adds £400-£800; dealer labour is significantly higher. 12-month warranty included on all rebuilt units through EnginesMarket.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLK 270 CDI or CLK 320 CDI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the OM612 five-cylinder and OM642 V6 are respected diesel engines. The OM642 V6 is renowned for its smooth power delivery but has known oil cooler seal failure. The OM612 five-cylinder is a cult favourite for its distinctive soundtrack but suffers from turbocharger wear. OM642 V6: smooth and torquey, but oil cooler seals fail at 80k-120k miles. OM612 five-cylinder: robust and characterful, but turbocharger bearing wear is common. Both engines can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles with proper maintenance. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What is the oil cooler seal problem on the Mercedes CLK 320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 engine has rubber oil cooler seals at the centre of the Vee that degrade and leak. Oil mixes with coolant or leaks externally, causing low oil pressure warnings and potential engine damage. Symptoms: low oil pressure warnings, oil in coolant, external oil leaks. Repair requires intake manifold removal - labour-intensive. Specialist seal replacement costs £700-£1,200. If ignored, engine damage can occur - catch it early.

mainEntity.name: What is the "Black Death" problem on the Mercedes CLK 270/320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: "Black Death" is the common term for injector seal failure on Mercedes CDI engines. When the seals fail, unburnt diesel and exhaust gases escape, creating a hard, tar-like carbon buildup around the injector seats. Symptoms: chuffing noise from engine bay, black residue around injectors. Affects both OM612 and OM642 engines. Specialist seal replacement costs £250-£450. Catch it early - the repair is far cheaper than engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLK 270/320 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained OM612 and OM642 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. The OM642 can achieve 150,000+ miles with oil cooler seals replaced once. The OM612 five-cylinder is known for exceptional longevity. OM612: 150k-200k+ miles with regular servicing. OM642: 150k+ miles but oil cooler seals need doing once. Injector seal failure typically occurs from 80,000-150,000 miles. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles significantly extends life.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes CLK 270/320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a CLK 270/320 CDI worth £2,500-£7,000, specialist engine replacement at £1,600-£3,200 is worthwhile if the body and interior are in excellent condition. However, if the car has rust, electrical issues, or poor bodywork, consider scrapping it. CLK values have stabilised at "rock bottom" prices. A clean, well-maintained CLK is worth saving. Rebuilt OM612/OM642 engines cost £1,600-£3,200 supply only. If the car has other major issues, replacement may not be cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: Mercedes CLK 270 CDI vs CLK 320 CDI - which engine is more reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 in the CLK 320 CDI offers more power and refinement but has the well-documented oil cooler seal weakness. The OM612 five-cylinder in the CLK 270 CDI is more characterful and robust but suffers from turbocharger wear. Both are reliable with proper maintenance. OM642 (CLK 320 CDI): 224 hp, smooth V6, but oil cooler seals fail. OM612 (CLK 270 CDI): 170 hp, distinctive five-cylinder, but turbo wear is common. Both engines can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles with proper maintenance. The OM642 is generally the more desirable engine for performance and refinement.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLK 270/320 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLK 270 CDI and CLK 320 CDI brought diesel power to the CLK range for the first time. The CLK 270 CDI arrived with the second-generation C209 in 2002, powered by the OM612 2.7-litre five-cylinder turbodiesel - a cult favourite among diesel enthusiasts. The CLK 320 CDI joined in 2005 with the facelift, featuring the OM642 3.0-litre V6 turbodiesel that delivered effortless torque and refined motorway cruising.

milestones.description: CLK 270 CDI launched with OM612 DE27 LA 2.7L five-cylinder turbodiesel, 170 hp, 400 Nm torque
Facelift: CLK 320 CDI introduced with OM642 DE30 LA 3.0L V6 turbodiesel, 224 hp, 415 Nm torque
CLK 270 CDI discontinued; replaced by CLK 320 CDI in diesel line-up
2009 - CLK 320 CDI produced throughout C209/A209 CLK range
CLK production ends; OM642 engine continues in other Mercedes models

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLK 270/320 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLK 270 CDI and CLK 320 CDI are powered by two of Mercedes' most respected diesel engines - the OM612 five-cylinder and the OM642 V6. The OM612 is a cult favourite for its distinctive five-cylinder soundtrack and robust construction, while the OM642 delivers effortless V6 refinement. Both have known weak points: the OM612 suffers from turbocharger bearing wear and injector seal leakage, while the OM642 is plagued by oil cooler seal failure and swirl flap linkage issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Failure - The Most Common CLK 320 CDI Problem
problems.rootCause: The rubber oil cooler seals at the centre of the Vee engine degrade and leak. Oil mixes with coolant or leaks externally, causing low oil pressure warnings and potential engine damage if ignored. The repair requires removal of the intake manifold, turbocharger, and numerous other components - making it a labour-intensive job.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of oil cooler seals, intake manifold removal, cleaning of EGR system and inlet ports
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles with genuine Mercedes upgraded seals

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement engine with new oil cooler seals, turbo, injectors tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles with all known OM642 weaknesses addressed

problems.recommendation: OM642 oil cooler seal failure is a well-documented issue. If you notice low oil pressure warnings, oil in the coolant, or external oil leaks from the centre of the Vee, get it inspected immediately. Specialist seal replacement at £700-£1,200 resolves the issue and prevents catastrophic engine failure. If the engine has been run low on oil, full replacement with a rebuilt unit is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes CLK 320 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: OM612 Turbocharger Failure - The CLK 270 CDI's Weakness
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger bearing can fail due to oil feed line contamination or oil starvation. Symptoms include loss of power, excessive smoke, whistling or screeching noises, and fault codes P0299 (boost pressure too low) or P0238 (turbocharger overboost).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and replace turbocharger with reconditioned unit, new oil feed lines, fresh oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: 100k-150k miles; effective if caught before engine damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt OM612 engine with new turbo, injectors, and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo debris has circulated through the engine

problems.recommendation: The OM612 five-cylinder is otherwise robust. If your CLK 270 CDI has lost power or is making unusual noises, get the turbo inspected immediately. Specialist turbo replacement at £900-£1,500 is cost-effective. However, if turbo debris has circulated through the engine, full replacement is the only safe route.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM612 Mercedes CLK 270 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Seal Failure ("Black Death") - Both OM612 and OM642
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes CLK 270 CDI (OM612) and CLK 320 CDI (OM642), 2002-2009
problems.rootCause: Injector seals fail, allowing unburnt diesel fuel and exhaust gases to escape past the seal. This creates a hard, tar-like carbon buildup around the injector seats - a condition commonly referred to as "Black Death." Symptoms include a chuffing noise from the engine bay, visible black residue around injectors, and rough running.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace injector seals, clean injector seats, new clamp bolts
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-150k miles; effective if caught before seat damage

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Injector Seat Re-cutting & Seal Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Re-cut injector seats, replace seals and clamp bolts with upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if seat damage has occurred; prevents recurrence

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt engine with new injectors, seals, and components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if Black Death has caused cylinder head damage or injector seizure

problems.recommendation: Injector seal failure is common across both OM612 and OM642 engines. Don't ignore the tell-tale chuffing noise or black residue. Specialist injector seal replacement at £250-£450 is cost-effective and resolves the issue. However, if the engine has been run with leaking seals for an extended period, cylinder head damage may have occurred - in which case a rebuilt engine with new injectors and upgraded seals is the safer option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM612/OM642 Mercedes CLK 270/320 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Swirl Flap Linkage Failure - OM642 Loss of Power
problems.rootCause: The plastic linkage rods in the intake manifold swirl flap system break, causing the flaps to stick. This results in loss of power, stumbling below 1,800 rpm, and increased fuel consumption. No fault codes are often stored - diagnosis requires live data monitoring.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace broken linkage rods with upgraded metal components
Replace complete intake manifold with swirl flaps
repairOptions.longevity: Required if flaps themselves are damaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement engine with new intake manifold, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if flap debris has entered cylinders

problems.recommendation: Loss of power and hesitation below 1,800 rpm are classic symptoms of swirl flap linkage failure. A £150-£300 repair kit with metal linkage rods is the definitive fix. If the flaps themselves are damaged, a replacement intake manifold at £500-£900 is required. Catch it early - flap debris in the cylinders can cause catastrophic engine damage.
